primitives.name: Field Access Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: No person allowed to walk up and down on side lines.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_{field}': 'dimensionless indicator function for field access', 't': 'time in seconds', 'x': 'spatial coordinate along sideline'}
primitives.assumptions: Spatial continuity of field boundaries, discrete time steps for access control.
primitives.breakdown_regime: x ∈ [0, L] where L is sideline length; A_{field}(x,t) = 0 implies prohibited access.

layer2.mapping: Field access control mirrors temporal constraint enforcement in game state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Observer count per unit time at sideline boundary

primitives.name: Penalty Enforcement Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the ball was In play when the offense occurred, the penaity shall be enforced frem the spot where the ball was put in play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_{penalty}': '15-yard penalty distance', 's_{inplay}': 'position vector of ball when in play', 's_{spot}': 'enforcement starting position vector'}
primitives.assumptions: Ball position is deterministically known at infraction moment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: s_{spot} = s_{inplay} if offense occurs during play; otherwise, default enforcement spot applies.

layer2.mapping: Penalty rule derives from game state transition kernel under violation condition.
layer2.telemetry: Distance between initial and final positions after penalty application

primitives.name: Offender Exclusion Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: The offender shali be excluded from the neighborhood of the field of play for the remainder of the game.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E_{exclusion}': 'exclusion event indicator', 'T_{game}': 'total game duration in seconds', 't_{infraction}': 'instant of infraction in seconds'}
primitives.assumptions: Exclusion is absolute and non-reversible until end of game.

layer2.mapping: Exclusion protocol mirrors strategic isolation in game-theoretic agent interaction models.
layer2.telemetry: Duration of exclusion period relative to total game time

Field access is modeled as a spatiotemporal exclusion map, where movement along sidelines is forbidden. Penalty enforcement operates as a conditional shift in game state, anchored to the ball’s last known position during play. Offender exclusion functions as a permanent strategic disruption, modeled as a binary event over time. These primitives form a dual structure: one governing real-time access dynamics and another governing post-violation state evolution. Their interplay defines a closed-loop game logic where each action triggers a measurable consequence. Failure modes include unauthorized access breaches, misapplication of penalties, and incomplete enforcement of exclusions. Each primitive exhibits a distinct regime: spatial (access), positional (penalty), and temporal (exclusion). The system's robustness depends on consistent enforcement of these regimes through referee authority.
